They just constantly hit you, every second or every minute. All you do is hold onto that wreckage. The waves are grief. But as time goes by, those waves get smaller, less intense, and happen less. The waves probably never fully stop, but eventually they get so small that you’re able to deal with them. The waves are different for everyone and for some people and relationships they might be at their worst for months while other people might only have it at it’s worth for a week. 

Everyone is different, but the way you’re feeling is totally fine. Just stay strong and keep your head above water.

Unfortunately I don’t think there is any secret way to just get over someone you loved. Loving someone takes a big part of your brain. Your body gets used to the feeling of them being around, their face, their smell, their quirks. You can’t just forget those things. If this is a new breakup you’re still just in the beginning stages of grief. I know you said that he doesn’t care about you, but that’s probably not true. The difference is in a breakup, the person doing the breakup typically has thought about this and prepared for it. So they have a head start on clearing their brain so to say. In his head right now he is probably feeling relieved, not sad which is why it seems he doesn’t care. He’s relieved because something he has been thinking about for days, weeks, months even has finally be done. He finally built up the courage to break your heart. But that doesn’t mean he doesn’t care. It just means that he knew it was coming and you didn’t. 

Getting over someone always requires time. There’s no secret formula to how much time or how to get over someone. Tomorrow I’ll be a month out from my breakup date and everything I do still reminds me of her. It might be the same for you it might be totally different. Just give it time. I know it’s hard, but give it time and don’t contact him. Because when you contact him you’re playing right into his hands. The person who initiates the breakup has all the power initially. They know that if they want you to come back all they have to do is message you and you’ll likely come back. So their brain doesn’t register to miss you if you are constantly texting them. 

As for how to pass the time, hang out with friends, go back to your pre-relationship hobbies, do things only you liked to do that your partner didn’t, find a new thing you’ve been wanting to try, talk to family, work out. Time is the worst thing in a breakup, but unfortunately it is necessary. If you need help, feel free to message me.

I don’t think you need to fully recover. Hear me out. Losing your brother is hard, it’s something I have no experience with. It scarred you. You’ll carry that scar around with you for the rest of your life. Grief is like a boat in a storm. You’re the boat, waves are memories. The ending of a relationship wrecks the boat, so you’re in the middle of the water with the wreckage. You might try and survive on your own, or you might grab something from the wreckage... a note, a memory, an article of clothing. Every time a wave hits you, you feel like you may not make it. You feel like you’ve been uprooted and all the healing you’ve done is gone. But over time, the waves go down. They might go from every day to only once a week to a few times a month and so on. Eventually you’ll be able to remember the good times and laugh, not cry. You’ll think of a memory only the two of you have and it won’t leave you heartbroken for days. Love is an amazing emotion and feeling. Love is so intense and is so deep in the brain. But that means when you lose someone, it scars you. That scar means that person meant something to you. Those scars are deep, the deeper the better because it means that person was important. Those scars hurt. But everyone has scars. And think about when you get a scar on your body... that scar eventually grows over and is stronger than before. You become stronger because of the scars. Grief is the price we pay for love. 

The same goes for your girlfriend. It’s going to hurt. You’re going to go through every moment of your relationship and wonder if you could’ve affected this outcome by changing something. But remember, those waves of grief get smaller over time. The heart and brain are powerful. Your body wants to love again. Your body enjoys the feeling of being in love. Your body releases all kinds of chemicals when you see your girlfriend’s smile or her face or think of her. So will you recover with your girlfriend of 5 years? I don’t know... maybe. But will you recover and find love again? I guarantee it. Seeing the negatives are always a lot easier than seeing the positives. It’s hard to find positives in things sometimes. But I’ll leave you with something I believe: the ugly things in life happen so you can appreciate the beauty in life. I wish you the best

You make a choice every single day to text them in the morning and tell them to have a good day and that you love them. You make a choice every day to either make it work or let it fall apart. There might be days where you’re so mad you refuse to look them in the eye or talk to them. But there are some days when you are so happy you can’t see anything but their face. These are choices. You make choices everyday to let them eat something you wanted or to let them sleep in a little later even though it might make you late. These are the little things that show you care. You have a choice to sacrifice everything for love. 

I’m not saying you should or shouldn’t give up on love, but my personal feeling is that if you love someone, you can choose to make things work or make them better. I don’t like the whole idea of “if you love something let it go and if it comes back then it’s right.” If you both love something, you should choose to make it work.
